pairs.why: A keeps the real booth's taller, straighter build with a gently curved roof and a soft, even finish, while B has a domed, puffier roof and reads more like a toy.
B adds a glowing halo, a chunky oversized handle and a purple base, so it looks more like a toy, while A stays closer to the real booth's plain red build and even lighting.
A's thick, soft rim and the shadow it casts on the striped wall come slightly closer to the real wall clock's depth than B's flatter, more graphic face.
B is a glossy, glowing clock standing on a floor ledge, which changes what the object is, while A stays a wall clock with a soft shadow like the real card.
B sets the clock on a floor with a ground shadow, while A matches the real card's wall-hung clock with a soft shadow.
A shows the controller large from a high three-quarter view with headphones resting in front, close to the real card, while B is small, seen from low and pushed off into the background.
